messages.author: a4c5d7d1c977b688
messages.subject: some weird error message
parts:
Dear Team,

I have encountered the following error:

> compiled <- compileNimble(model, mcmc)
Compiling
  [Note] This may take a minute.
  [Note] Use 'showCompilerOutput = TRUE' to see C++ compilation details.
Error in file(con, open = "w") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In dir.create(dirName) :
  cannot create dir 'C:\Users\QING~1.ZHA\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmpqs5udP\nimble_generatedCode', reason 'No such file or directory'
2: In file(con, open = "w") :
  cannot open file 'C:\Users\QING~1.ZHA\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmpqs5udP\nimble_generatedCode\P_1_code_MID_1.h': No such file or directory

Everything up to this point seems to be alright. More importantly, I have run the same model with fewer (1000) iterations and it worked just fine. Now I'm trying to run it with 300,000 iterations and see this error. Does anyone know why this is happening and how to prevent it? Thank you.

Best,
Qing

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: some weird error message
parts:
Hi Qing,

That is odd if you were able to run a shorter MCMC but not the longer one.

When we compile models or algorithms, we create a subdirectory called `nimble_generatedCode` within R's temp directory for the current R session. The path to R's temp directory can be found by running `tempdir()` in your R session.

1) So before you run `compileNimble(model,mcmc)`, you might check that `C:\Users\QING~1.ZHA\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmpqs5udP` exists (but be careful when you do this to replace "Rtmpqs5udP" with the actual temp dir for your current R session). 

2) After the error occurs, you might run `traceback()` and see if that gives any useful error messages.  Also check at this point if `C:\Users\QING~1.ZHA\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmpqs5udP` exists.

3) As a work around, you might be able to set `dirName` in your call to `compileNimble` to point to some other directory that exists and see if Nimble is able to create `nimble_generatedCode` in that other directory. See `help(compileNimble)` for more details.

-chris

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: some weird error message
parts:
hi Qing,

You should not use the same directory for different R sessions. So, yes, try creating a separate directory for each of your R sessions. It sounds like you have one model per session, so that means you'll have a separate directory for each model, e.g., c:/R_temp_dir_model1, c:/R_temp_dir_model2, etc.

Given that the original error message indicated a problem with accessing `C:\Users\QING~1.ZHA\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmpqs5udP` and/or creating `C:\Users\QING~1.ZHA\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmpqs5udP\nimble_generatedCode`, as an additional check, before you run `compileNimble`, from within R, check that R can access the directory you're using for that R session. 

```
i <- 1  # for first model

thisDirName <- paste0("c:/R_temp_dir_model", i)

### Steps to check ability to access directory and create subdirectory
print(dir.exists(thisDirName))   # this assumes you've created the directory outside of R
print(list.files(thisDirName)) 
testDir <- file.path(thisDirName, 'test'))
print(dir.create(testDir))      # test that R can create a subdirectory, since nimble will try to create `nimble_generatedCode`

compiled <- compileNimble(model, mcmc, dirName=thisDirName)
```

-chris
